entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
François Watrin was a French infantry commander during the French Revolutionary Wars.

 Born in Beauvais, France on January 29, 1772, Watrin rose through the ranks of the French military, distinguishing himself in the Siege of Toulon (1793) and the Battle of the Pyramids (1798).

 As a key figure in the early years of the French Republic, Watrin played a role in shaping the country's military strategy and contributing to the eventual defeat of the French monarchy.

 Despite his significant contributions, Watrin's life was cut short when he died on November 22, 1802, at the age of 30.

 "We must not forget the sacrifices of those who fought for our freedom," Watrin once said in a letter to his brother, highlighting the enduring importance of his legacy.
